reasons: F01, F02, F03: a material weakness in financial close/reporting is disclosed and there is no auditor ICFR attestation (likely a smaller reporting company), so control over period-end entries is weak and unverified.

R08, R10, R19: total accruals are about 35% of total assets, RSST accruals are 0.36, and operating cash flow is the opposite sign to net income (-1.02x). Reported earnings are almost entirely accrual-driven and not backed by cash.
R09, R03: the Beneish M-score of -0.67 is well above the -1.78 threshold, driven in part by an asset quality index of 1.48 (more capitalised or soft assets).
R13, F22: soft assets make up 83% of total assets, and a major acquisition happened in the year. Goodwill, intangible and purchase-accounting estimates leave a lot of room for judgment.
R15, R04: ROA changed by +0.6 even though sales fell (SGI 0.88). A large earnings swing during a revenue decline points to one-off or accrual items rather than operating performance.

F11, F14, F20, F21: material related-party transactions, a CEO/CFO change during the year, incentive pay tied to revenue/EPS, and a capital raise create both pressure and opportunity to manage results.
F26, F28: emphasis on non-GAAP measures and a segment/reporting change can hide comparability problems.

R17, F07, F16, F17, F24: mitigating factors: the Dechow F-score (0.4) is below its threshold, there is no prior-period correction, no SEC inquiry and no class action, and no going-concern doubt or auditor change was reported.
